text:
ana: Hey all, day 1! I'm on a company-managed Pixelbook (ChromeOS) and I can connect the WireGuard profile in the OS. Browsing internal docs in Chrome works, but the Linux (Crostini) terminal can't `git clone` or `docker pull` from our internal registry. Anyone dealt with Crostini + company VPN?
it-support: Welcome Ana! Yep, Crostini runs in a lightweight VM and ChromeOS VPNs don't always route into the container by default. The host (chrome) sees the VPN routes but the container's network is NATed behind a VM interface.
carla: Two pragmatic workarounds that usually help: 1) Run an SSH SOCKS proxy from the ChromeOS host to the bastion and point your Crostini apps at that proxy. 2) Forward specific ports from host -> container (socat) for registry or git if you only need a couple services.
nana: Sounds good, can you paste the exact steps for #1? I'm not super comfy with low-level networking.
devops: From ChromeOS (not inside the Linux terminal) open the Secure Shell app or crosh "vmc start termina" then run an SSH tunnel to the bastion: `ssh -i /path/to/key -D 1080 alice@bastion.redwood -N` Keep it running.
devops: Crostini's host IP is typically 100.115.92.1 (container usually 100.115.92.2). In your Linux container export the proxy to point at the host: `export HTTP_PROXY=http://100.115.92.1:1080` and `export HTTPS_PROXY=http://100.115.92.1:1080` then try `git clone` / `curl`.
carla: For docker inside Crostini, Docker-in-Crostini can be fiddly. If you run Docker in the container, set `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` in the container systemd service or use `docker --config` for client pulls. Alternatively, forward the registry port from host into the container: on ChromeOS host (crosh) you can run `socat TCP-LISTEN:5000,fork,reuseaddr TCP:10.240.2.10:5000` (replace with internal registry IP) and then access localhost:5000 from the container.
it-support: TL;DR: quick test path: 1) ssh -D on host to bastion, 2) in Crostini `export HTTP_PROXY` to host IP and test `git clone`/`curl`, 3) if registry used by docker, either configure docker proxy or forward port with socat.
nana: Tried the SSH SOCKS approach. From ChromeOS shell: `ssh -i /mnt/stateful_partition/ssh_keys/id_ed25519 -D 1080 alice@bastion.redwood -N` Then inside Crostini `export HTTPS_PROXY=http://100.115.92.1:1080` and `git clone git@git.redwood.internal:repo.git` hung at auth (ssh) 
carla: For git+ssh you need to forward the ssh agent or use the host's SSH socket. Easiest: in Crostini set up an ssh config that proxies through the SOCKS proxy using `ProxyCommand nc -x 100.115.92.1:1080 %h %p` or use `ProxyJump` via a host-side jump. Example `~/.ssh/config` entry: `Host bastion.redwood
  HostName bastion.redwood
  ProxyCommand nc -x 100.115.92.1:1080 %h %p`
devops: If netcat (nc) doesn't have SOCKS support, use `proxychains` or install `tsocks`. Another trick: do `ssh -A -J alice@bastion.redwood your-internal-host` from the host and then connect from the container to the host forwarded port.
nana: Ok I used `ProxyCommand` and `git clone` worked! Docker still needs a little more. I tried `socat` on the host to forward 5000 to the registry and then `docker pull localhost:5000/core/base:latest` from the container and it pulled successfully.
it-support: Nice. We'll capture these steps in the onboarding doc for Chromebook users. Two notes: 1) host IP (100.115.92.1) can vary slightly across ChromeOS versions, run `ip addr show` in the container to confirm gateway. 2) Keep your SSH tunnel process alive in the host background or use the Secure Shell app which can run persistently.
infra-bot: Docs: https://confluence.redwood/infra/chromeos-crostini-vpn-workarounds and internal snippet: "Use host SSH SOCKS proxy + point Crostini HTTP/HTTPS to host IP (typically 100.115.92.1) OR forward specific ports via socat" :white_check_mark:
nana: This solved everything, thanks!! I'll paste exact commands I used into the onboarding checklist.
carla: Awesome welcome and congrats on day 1 :party-parrot:
nana: Thanks team :)
